task.description: Confirm root-cause diagnosis for ISS-0612 / GH #556: src/db/provisioning.zig advisory-lock release can leave a lock held by an idle pooled connection, hanging full-suite zig build test. ISS-0612 already documents extensive prior analysis (3 candidate mechanisms). ORCH pre-investigation during this run already ELIMINATED candidate #2 (defer ordering is correct -- empirically verified: releaseAdvisoryLock defer, registered after pool.release defer, correctly runs FIRST per Zig LIFO semantics) and NARROWED toward candidate #1: provisionTenantSchema (src/db/provisioning.zig:117-125) calls releaseAdvisoryLock(lock_conn, tenant_id_str) catch {} -- if this exec fails for ANY reason (including conn._is_valid already being false, in which case Conn.exec at pool.zig:479 returns PoolError.StaleConnection WITHOUT ever sending the SQL to Postgres), the failure is silently swallowed and the connection proceeds to pool.release() afterward. The open question is: what sets conn._is_valid = false (or otherwise causes the unlock exec to fail) between acquireAdvisoryLock succeeding and releaseAdvisoryLock running, while the physical Postgres backend is still alive and the session-scoped lock is still held server-side? Also verify whether pool.release() bears any responsibility (it calls resetConnectionSearchPath but has zero awareness of advisory locks -- confirmed by direct source read of pool.zig:834-873). Produce a definitive, reproducible root cause -- ideally with a minimal repro (a small test or script that reliably triggers the idle-lock-holder state) rather than code-reading inference alone, since the original discovery was from a live hang during a full-suite run, not a targeted repro.
acceptance_criteria: Root cause is confirmed via reproduction (not just code-reading inference)
The exact code path that leaves conn holding the lock is identified with file:line precision
docs/issues/ISS-0612.json updated with the confirmed root cause

result.summary: Confirmed root cause for ISS-0612: src/db/provisioning.zig:117-125's session-scoped advisory-lock block closes (acquires AND releases the lock, returns lock_conn to the pool) BEFORE Steps 2-6a of provisionTenantSchema() execute -- so the lock does not serialize the pass as its own comment (lines 104-105) claims. Concurrent same-tenant provisionTenantSchema() calls race unprotected through Steps 2-6a, contending on migrations.zig's single GLOBAL (not per-tenant) advisory-lock key (MIGRATIONS_LOCK_KEY_SQL, migrations.zig:31-32/463) and on a third, independent per-schema advisory lock inside the bpm_provision_tenant_schema() SQL function (migrations/060_schema_per_tenant_bootstrap.sql:89). The originally-suspected mechanism (conn._is_valid flipping false between acquireAdvisoryLock succeeding and releaseAdvisoryLock running) was ruled out via direct source read of Conn.exec (pool.zig:467-488): no path both sets _is_valid=false and returns success, and nothing touches lock_conn between the two calls. Confirmed empirically via a targeted stress reproduction (12 threads, same tenant_id, shared Pool pool_size=3, tests/integration/iss0129_migration_run_advisory_lock_test.zig, temporarily appended then reverted): progress stalled at 24/96 calls and never recovered within a 180s hard cap; force-terminated workers returned error.PoolExhausted (8/12), confirming pool connections became stuck checked-out under same-tenant concurrent provisioning load with zero server-side advisory locks or active queries observed at sample time -- consistent with the unprotected-Steps-2-6a race, not the _is_valid theory.
